title: Web Design + Code 1
tagline: Peel Up the Pixels. Brick by brick. Tag by tag. Source-level fluency.

plos.title: Visual Vocabulary
plos.text: Achieve fluency in design's visual language.

plos.title: Technical Skills
plos.text: Demonstrate proficiency in relevant design skills.

objectives.title: Apply Graphic Design Principles to Web Interfaces
objectives.text: Incorporate layout, typography, and color principles into web design projects to build a visually coherent interface a reader can follow.

objectives.title: Read the Web as a Made Thing
objectives.text: Inspect how pages are built, and explain the choices and tools behind them, including AI assistance, on a platform that keeps changing.

objectives.title: Design for Accessibility and Inclusivity
objectives.text: Apply WCAG-based practices so pages work for people of diverse abilities: meaningful structure, text alternatives, keyboard access, visible focus, and layouts that reflow.

objectives.title: Write HTML and CSS by Hand
objectives.text: Write clean, valid, semantic HTML and CSS, and explain and modify any code you submit.

objectives.title: Implement Responsive Design Principles
objectives.text: Apply responsive design techniques, including media queries, Flexbox, and CSS Grid, so layouts adapt across devices and screen sizes.

objectives.title: Use Version Control and Browser Tools
objectives.text: Use GitHub to keep one repository, commit changes, and publish a working site, and use browser developer tools to locate a fault, predict a change, and verify the result.

objectives.title: Direct and Evaluate AI Assistance
objectives.text: Use AI assistance only within the stage an assignment allows, evaluate its output against the source, the browser, and documentation, and explain and revise any code you keep.

weeks.title: Peel up the pixels
weeks.summary: Look beneath a designed surface; change one element and explain its effect.
outcomes: State what Canvas, the course site, and your repository each hold.
Predict what a Markdown mark will change. Make the change without AI. Compare the preview with your prediction.
Accept the Workspace assignment. Commit a first edit in your own private repository.
Answer the four introduction questions in Markdown in your repository. Submit the repository link.

weeks.title: Give content a structure
weeks.summary: Build Project 1 with headings, ordered steps, meaningful links, and an image you can credit.
outcomes: Structure the recipe with meaningful headings, unordered ingredients, and ordered steps.
Explain the recipe list choice after moving one step outside its list in a copy.
Credit one permitted recipe image with purposeful alternative text and a descriptive source link.
Test the recipe source link, image, and latest saved HTML before delivery.

weeks.title: Make the structure visible
weeks.summary: Use CSS to create hierarchy and breathing room, then demonstrate an independent change.
outcomes: Explain how a selector and declaration create the recipe type hierarchy and spacing.
Predict a margin or padding change, make it without AI, and compare the visible result.
Publish a readable recipe whose headings, lists, image credit, and source link survive narrow widths.
Repair a supplied nesting or class-name fault without AI and verify the saved result.

weeks.title: Build a place for your work
weeks.summary: Migrate one page manually, publish it, and plan Project 2 in Figma.
outcomes: Trace a relative path from the tribute file to the recipe folder and test the destination.
Commit, push, and verify one manual recipe change on its published page.
Plan the real tribute content and reading order in one wide Figma frame.
Credit two tribute sources beside the planned content and one permitted image.
Ask AI to explain one tribute path or commit message, then check its answer against documentation.

weeks.title: Arrange the pieces
weeks.summary: Use flexible layout for Project 2 and practice fixing one rule at a time.
outcomes: Arrange the tribute figure and introduction with Flexbox while preserving meaningful source order.
Predict how removing flex-wrap affects the tribute at 375px, then restore the safer behavior.
Repair one observed tribute layout problem and verify it at narrow and wide widths.
Publish the tribute with readable content, working sources, keyboard focus, and a route home.

weeks.title: Build a repeatable pattern
weeks.summary: Build Project 3 from reusable classes; consolidate known layout skills on October 28.
outcomes: Build three field-guide entries from one reusable semantic card pattern.
Predict and test gap and column changes at 375px and 1000px.
Explain which media-query rule applies at each tested width from browser evidence.
Name an exact blocker after two focused repair attempts on the practice starter.

sessions.title: Project 3: one card becomes a system

weeks.title: Let the page respond
weeks.summary: Repair the practice together and adapt Project 3 as space and reading needs change.
outcomes: Choose a field-guide breakpoint where its cards or navigation begin to crowd.
Build a semantic guide section and repair one selector or path fault without AI.
Test the field guide anchors, focus, images, and text at narrow, intermediate, and wide widths.
Explain the active responsive rule immediately below and above the chosen breakpoint.
Accept one AI completion in the field guide, test it in the browser, and explain the line you kept.

weeks.title: Debug and publish Project 3
weeks.summary: Use browser evidence to locate a fault and deliver Project 3 as a small, usable responsive page.
outcomes: Locate one field-guide fault using browser or source evidence before changing code.
Repair the fault, reproduce its original test, and check one neighboring condition.
Publish a responsive field guide with three accurate entries, reliable navigation, credits, and keyboard focus.
Verify the public guide signed out at narrow, intermediate, and wide widths.
Set a written scope for AI code in the field guide, test the result, and revise one part yourself.

weeks.title: Design a clear invitation
weeks.summary: Create Project 4, a concise page that tells one audience what it offers and what to do next.
outcomes: State the landing page audience, offering, and primary action in three concise sentences.
Plan the real landing page content at 375px and 1280px in Figma.
Build one semantic landing-page structure with a flexible hero or feature group.
Explain how the same HTML changes arrangement between widths after one peer revision.

sessions.title: From two Figma frames to one flexible page

weeks.title: Make interactions honest
weeks.summary: Make calls to action and an optional form practice understandable, keyboard usable, and truthful.
outcomes: Choose a link, button, or labeled form that matches the actual landing page behavior.
Reach and activate the primary landing page action by keyboard with visible focus.
State the expected and observed action result, including whether it sends any data.
Repair one misleading interaction or confirm its destination at a narrow width.

sessions.title: Links, forms, focus, and reduced motion

weeks.title: Finish, test, and curate
weeks.summary: Finish Project 4 December 2, then curate existing work and prepare to explain it.
outcomes: Repair the highest-impact landing page failure and verify the published result signed out.
Publish the landing page with a truthful primary action, working links, readable layouts, and visible focus.
Curate four project entries with introductions, working return paths, credits, and a repository link.
Explain and modify one source decision independently during the portfolio presentation.
Commit the final portfolio version and test every project link while signed out.
